Use SingleCellExperiment and AnnData data

31 October, 2026

Source: vignettes/use_sce_and_anndata_data.Rmd
use_sce_and_anndata_data.Rmd

Overview

Cerebro does not need a Seurat object. A .crb file is the common format, and three kinds of input lead to it:

You have Convert with
Seurat object (.rds, .qs2) convertSeuratToCerebro()
SingleCellExperiment (.rds, .qs2) convertSCEToCerebro()
AnnData / scanpy file (.h5ad), MuData (.h5mu) convertH5adToCerebro()

Because .crb is the hub, the formats also convert into each other: a Seurat object can be written as .h5ad for scanpy, an .h5ad file can be turned into a SingleCellExperiment, and so on. AnnData files are read natively with rhdf5; no Python is needed.

From an AnnData file 

library(CerebroNexus)

crb <- convertH5adToCerebro(
  "pbmc.h5ad",
  result_dir = "cerebro",
  groups = c("louvain", "sample"),
  organism = "Human"
)

This takes what scanpy stored, not only the matrix:

  • the embeddings in obsm (X_umap, X_pca, …) as projections;
  • the ranked marker genes from sc.tl.rank_genes_groups;
  • scanpy’s category colours (uns["<column>_colors"]);
  • Visium coordinates and tissue images (obsm["spatial"], uns["spatial"]), one spatial section per library;
  • scirpy TCR/BCR tables (airr argument) and PAGA / scVelo / pseudotime trajectories.

Use use_raw = TRUE for adata.raw, modality = to pick one modality of an .h5mu file, and gene_names = to name genes by a var column when the index holds Ensembl IDs.

From a SingleCellExperiment 

crb <- convertSCEToCerebro(
  "sce.rds",
  result_dir = "cerebro",
  assay = "logcounts",
  groups = c("cluster", "sample")
)

From a SpatialData store 

crb <- convertSpatialDataToCerebro(
  "visium.zarr",
  result_dir = "cerebro",
  groups = c("region", "in_tissue"),
  organism = "Mouse"
)

The cell table, the coordinates and the tissue pictures are read from the .zarr directory, with one spatial section per region. Coordinates come from obsm["spatial"] when the table has them (Visium) and from the shapes the table annotates otherwise (MERFISH, Xenium). Stores compressed with Blosc (lz4, zstd or zlib), zstd or gzip are read; a store that needs another codec stops with the codec’s name. Blosc chunks are decoded in R, lz4 (the numcodecs default) at about 4 MB/s, so re-save a large store with zstd, or use an .h5ad file.

Back to scanpy 

exportToH5ad("cerebro/cerebro_pbmc.crb", "pbmc_back.h5ad")
import anndata as ad
adata = ad.read_h5ad("pbmc_back.h5ad")

Expression, cell metadata, projections, marker genes, category colours and, for spatial data, coordinates and tissue images are written. A message lists what .h5ad has no place for (immune repertoire, trajectories, trees, …).

In the Builder

launchCerebroBuilder() accepts .h5ad, .h5mu, a .zip of a SpatialData .zarr folder, and SingleCellExperiment .rds / .qs2 files like Seurat ones, and offers PAGA, scVelo and pseudotime trajectories next to monocle2. Spatial coordinates arrive as one spatial section per library_id, and Visium tissue pictures are attached to their sections as images at the position their scale factor gives.
